name: Keylogging
description:
Adversaries may log user keystrokes to intercept credentials or other information from the user as the user types them.

Some methods of keylogging include:

* Masquerading as a legitimate third-party keyboard to record user keystrokes.(Citation: Zeltser-Keyboard) On both Android and iOS, users must explicitly authorize the use of third-party keyboard apps. Users should be advised to use extreme caution before granting this authorization when it is requested.
* Abusing accessibility features. On Android, adversaries may abuse accessibility features to record keystrokes by registering an `AccessibilityService` class, overriding the `onAccessibilityEvent` method, and listening for the `AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED` event type. The event object passed into the function will contain the data that the user typed. 
*Additional methods of keylogging may be possible if root access is available.

references.description: Lenny Zeltser. (2016, July 30). Security of Third-Party Keyboard Apps on Mobile Devices. Retrieved December 21, 2016.

telemetry.name: API Calls
telemetry.description: Instrumented mobile API calls and results relevant to an application behavior.
telemetry.collection_focus: Instrument selected APIs in the owned test app or approved research build; log caller, API, sanitized argument class and return status.

providers.name: Android logcat
providers.scope: Permitted logs from a consented test device/emulator; output depends on build, permissions and instrumentation.

providers.name: Android dumpsys
providers.scope: Point-in-time service/package state on an authorized development device.

providers.name: Instrumented test application
providers.scope: Own-app permission, API and state callbacks; not universal visibility into other apps.

configuration: Use a disposable emulator or owned development device with approved debugging. Record OS/API level, app version and instrumentation privileges.
Collect only relevant logcat buffers/tags and service snapshots; add explicit own-app instrumentation for events absent from OS logs.
Forward sanitized logs and compare before/after state. Remove test data and revoke debugging access after the lab session.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Android tooling does not imply iOS coverage. Standard mobile apps cannot observe all other apps or protected OS internals; MDM status is not full API, filesystem or content telemetry.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per owned device, app version and permission state: unexpected API/permission changes, background activity and network destinations. OS privacy restrictions and emulator differences limit observability.

telemetry.name: Network Traffic Content
telemetry.description: Packet or decoded application-protocol content visible at a network sensor.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope approved packet capture/protocol content collection to the lab flow; retain capture provenance and truncation indicators.

providers.name: Zeek
providers.scope: Connection and protocol metadata from traffic visible to the sensor.

providers.name: Suricata EVE
providers.scope: Configured flow, alert, DNS, HTTP, TLS and protocol records.

configuration: Use an authorized lab TAP/SPAN, virtual mirror or gateway interface. Define which traffic crosses it; avoid assuming visibility into every segment.
Enable the required Zeek analyzers or Suricata EVE event types. Export logs with sensor identity, clock synchronization and flow correlation identifiers.
Monitor capture loss, truncation and exporter sampling. Capture payload only with approval and restrictive retention; encryption normally prevents plaintext inspection.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Flows are not packet payloads. NAT, asymmetric routes, encryption, missing mirrors and sampling can hide attribution or content. A destination connection alone does not prove malicious intent.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per source and observation point: connection rate, destination-host/port fan-out, response/failure ratio and previously unseen destinations. Compare equivalent time windows; separate authorized scanners, NAT and sampling effects.

analytics.name: Analytic 1751
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Keylogging by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate API Calls via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED received by listener NOT IN $AccessibilityAllowList$ at rate > $KeystrokeEventThreshold$ per minute with source_apps spanning > $AppMonitorCountThreshold$ distinct apps]; Network Traffic Content via Enterprise Secure Web Gateway / Proxy [DNS/HTTP(S) inspection or proxy transaction metadata where enterprise decryption/inspection is deployed]; Permissions Request via Android Enterprise DPC / Application Vetting [DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionGrantState(); PackageManager manifest/requested-permission review]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: Approved assistive tech only. Minimal list.
Default 50 events/min — human typing baseline. Derive by measurement.
Default 3 distinct source apps — keylogger monitors broadly; assistive tech monitors narrowly.
Default 1KB — keystroke logs are small and dense.

log_sources.name: mobile:DynamicAnalysis
log_sources.channel: Dynamic API/runtime trace: AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED received by listener NOT IN $AccessibilityAllowList$ at rate > $KeystrokeEventThreshold$ per minute with source_apps spanning > $AppMonitorCountThreshold$ distinct apps

log_sources.name: webproxy:applog
log_sources.channel: DNS/HTTP(S) inspection or proxy transaction metadata where enterprise decryption/inspection is deployed

analytics.name: Analytic 1752
analytics.guidance: For iOS, detect Keylogging by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Application State via Apple MDM [InstalledApplicationList / ManagedApplicationList]; Network Traffic Flow via Apple Network Extension / Enterprise VPN [NEFilterFlow / per-app VPN / secure-web-gateway flow metadata]; Permissions Request via Application Vetting [Code-signing entitlements and Info.plist privacy usage-description keys]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: Known vendor cloud endpoints per approved keyboard.
Default 10KB per session — keystroke logs are small but dense.

log_sources.name: iOS:NetworkExtension
log_sources.channel: NEFilterFlow / per-app VPN / secure-web-gateway flow metadata

log_sources.name: mobile:ApplicationVetting
log_sources.channel: Code-signing entitlements and Info.plist privacy usage-description keys
